question.prompt: A red-bordered triangle holding three curved arrows chasing each other means…

options.text: You have priority all the way through the junction ahead
Traffic merges from the left ahead

question.explanation: Three curved arrows in a warning triangle: a roundabout is coming. Slow down and start looking to your right early.

question.prompt: A blue circle holding three arrows chasing each other means…

options.text: Mini-roundabout — treat it like any other roundabout
A one-way system you may enter from any side
You have priority over traffic already on it

question.explanation: A mini-roundabout is still a roundabout: give way to traffic coming from your immediate right, and signal as normal.

steps.title: The painted circle
steps.body: A mini-roundabout is a white circle painted on the road. Drive round it, not across it, and give way to your right.

question.prompt: You meet a white painted circle in the middle of a small junction. What is it?

options.text: A mini-roundabout — give way to traffic from your right
A no-waiting area you must keep clear
A marking you may drive straight over to save time

question.explanation: The painted circle is the roundabout. Go round it unless your vehicle is physically too long to do so.

steps.title: Choosing your lane
steps.body: Turning left or going ahead: approach in the left lane. Turning right or going full circle: approach in the right lane, signalling right.

question.prompt: You're turning right at a roundabout. Which lane, and which signal?

options.text: Right-hand lane, signalling right on the approach
Left-hand lane, because you always join on the left
Either lane — position doesn't matter on a roundabout

question.explanation: Your lane and signal tell everyone else where you're going. Get both right before you reach the give-way line.

steps.title: Straight ahead
steps.prompt: Put a straight-ahead roundabout in order, from approach to exit.

items.text: Approach in the left lane, giving no signal
Give way to traffic coming from your immediate right
Pass the exit before the one you want
Signal left, then leave at your exit

steps.explanation: Going straight ahead you signal nothing on the approach. The left signal comes only after you pass the exit before yours.

steps.scene: A long lorry is ahead of you at the roundabout. It's in the left-hand lane but positioned well over to the right.

options.text: It's turning right, so you can safely pass on its left
It may swing wide and take an unusual course — keep well back
The driver has made a mistake and will move over

question.explanation: A long vehicle needs the whole road to get round. Its position doesn't tell you where it's going — hang back and read the indicators.

steps.wrongBelief: Once you're on a roundabout you can cross to your exit without checking behind.

options.text: It's right — traffic on the roundabout has priority
Someone may be on your left, going further round than you
You have to stop before every exit

question.explanation: Cyclists, riders and motorcyclists often keep left all the way round. Mirror and blind spot before you cut across to your exit.

steps.repairNote: Check your left mirror and blind spot before leaving a roundabout — someone may be staying on it, on your inside.
